note: Authored teaching content for the Roles tab (v3, five roles). Merged at runtime with the live frontmatter from GET /api/agents, which is the source of truth for tools and model. Commands follow docs/SPEC.md §3; file names follow §4. `short` is the one-line description the light page shows; the dark page uses `purpose`.

roles.title: Rover
roles.purpose: Two of them, rover-1 and rover-2: each is spawned fresh every sol with a shell and nothing else, drives up to two tiles, scans, and rescues the astronaut when it is standing on the tile — and when rough terrain breaks it down, a note through the engine is its only way to ask the engineer for help.

actions.runs: Bash · python engine/engine.py act rover-1 move D5
Bash · python engine/engine.py act rover-1 scan
Bash · python engine/engine.py act rover-1 rescue

cannot.what: Give an order or resolve the sol
cannot.why: order and resolve are Mission Control's; role_guard.py denies them to a rover
the engine answers: rover-2 is broken at D4; needs an engineer repair

cannot.what: Leave a note as someone else
cannot.why: role_guard.py only accepts note <its own unit> …, so it cannot speak for rover-2

cannot.what: Decide what happens after a rescue — the human does (AskUserQuestion)
cannot.why: a rescue puts the team in phase: awaiting-orders; act, order, note and resolve are all refused until the officer on duty answers continue-mission, rest or abort-mission

roles.point: Tools: Bash — one line on the belt. Everything a rover does is one engine command, and its only way to talk is a note.
roles.short: Can be spawned more than once. Drives across tiles to explore, scans, and picks up the colonist.

roles.title: Engineer
roles.purpose: Reads the notes and the team state, then drops one repair file per broken rover — it has no shell at all, so a file in game/field/ is its only way to change the world, and a hook validates the file the moment it lands.

cannot.why: its tools: line is Read, Write — there is no Bash on this belt

cannot.what: Repair a rover that is not broken
cannot.why: field-check rejects the file and validate_build.py deletes it again

cannot.what: Back-date a repair to an earlier sol
cannot.why: field-check requires sol == the current sol

roles.point: No Bash. The engineer changes the world by writing a file where a hook is waiting for it.
roles.short: Repairs a broken rover by writing one file. No shell.

roles.title: Life Support
roles.purpose: Keeps the oxygen ledger: one file, one word — normal or conserve — and a PostToolUse hook runs the engine command on its behalf, because this role is deliberately denied a shell.

cannot.why: its own agent file wires write_scope.py --deny-all on Bash — this is the red row in the demo
role_guard.py: life-support may not run 'act rover-1 move C3'

cannot.what: Conserve two sols in a row
cannot.why: the engine refuses: conserve mode used last sol; astronaut must breathe

roles.point: The deny hook lives inside this agent's own file, not in settings.json — permissions can be per-worker.
roles.short: Sets the oxygen mode, normal or conserve, by editing one file. No shell.

roles.title: Navigator
roles.purpose: The only role with a memory: it diffs the tiles explored this sol against what it wrote last time and leaves one to three lessons with coordinates — in its own memory store, which survives /clear, and in game/intel/lessons.md, which the next Mission Control reads.

actions.handled_by: write_scope.py → memory: project in its frontmatter

cannot.why: write_scope.py in its frontmatter allows game/intel and its own memory directory, nothing more
no Bash on the belt, and role_guard.py would deny act anyway
protect_truth.py refuses game/truth.json for every agent, this session included

roles.point: State vs knowledge: the engine remembers where the rovers are, the Navigator remembers what the ground was like.
roles.short: Remembers the terrain: writes lessons to its own memory for the next sol.

roles.title: Mission Log
roles.purpose: Writes the sol's dispatch — 60 to 90 words naming the units, the notes and any BLOCKED incident — the one role whose output is written for people rather than for the engine, which is why it runs on Sonnet.

cannot.why: write_scope.py game/dispatches.md — one path, and that is the whole allowlist
it has no Bash, so it cannot act, order or resolve — it only reports

roles.point: Same harness, bigger model: the dispatch is the only artefact a human reads, so this role gets Sonnet.
roles.short: Writes the sol's dispatch for people to read. Runs on Sonnet.

roles.title: You
roles.purpose: The officer on duty. Decides after every rescue: continue, rest, or abort.

actions.runs: AskUserQuestion · 1 - Continue rescue mission / 2 - Rest and repair / 3 - Abort mission
Bash · python engine/engine.py continue-mission | rest | abort-mission

guards: the engine: act, order, note and resolve are refused while phase = awaiting-orders

cannot.why: after a rescue the engine refuses every mutating command until one of the three orders is given
run-sol stops the loop and asks — the answer is logged as kind:"decision", from human

roles.point: The sixth column is not an agent. A rescue hands control back to the room: the model reports, the human chooses.
roles.short: Decides after every rescue: continue, rest, or abort.
